[← Back to the lesson: Corpus preparation](../corpus-preparation.qmd)

## Check your understanding

1. Why does a random split of text chunks not guarantee independence between train and test?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

Chunks from the same document, source, or family may appear in multiple partitions. The split unit must match the generalization claim being tested, and overlap must then be audited.

</details>

2. Why freeze the tokenizer after fitting it on the training partition?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

To prevent its vocabulary or rules from incorporating information from texts reserved for validation or test in a held-out experiment.

</details>

3. Is deduplication always beneficial?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

No. It can reduce over-representation, but it can also alter the corpus distribution or remove legitimate repetitions. The method and its effects should be documented.

</details>

4. What information should accompany the token stream handed to the next stage?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

At minimum, corpus provenance, the exact tokenizer revision, encoding parameters, useful statistics, and document-boundary rules.

</details>
